methodology: Confirmed All comments, expanded the Yu-Fen Ceng and 吳立志 threads and every other visible reply control, and scrolled to the end. Fifty-one unique source IDs were retrieved: 34 top-level comments and 17 replies, including eight comments with attachments. Those attachments were inspected in the browser.
coverageNote: The page displayed 58 comments, but only 51 readable entries were retrieved. Seven could not be matched to source IDs or text. Six notices say a comment being replied to was deleted. Multiple notices may refer to the same missing comment, so they do not establish six distinct deletions or fully explain the seven-entry gap. Unknown wording, authors, times, removal actors and reasons are not reconstructed.
relationshipNote: Comments are grouped by comment_id in the source URL, with replies following the known root in displayed time order. Indentation indicates a reply group, not a precise parent or full chain length. Platform reply labels are retained and deletion notices noted; unverified exact parentId values remain null.
timeNote: Times follow Facebook’s display, converted to Taiwan time (UTC+8) with minute precision and no invented seconds. 12 a.m. is treated as 00:00. Edited flags are interface observations without full edit times or history. Reading was sequential, not an atomic snapshot.
reactionNote: “Liked by author” describes the interface state, not acceptance of every argument. Criticism, concessions, support and short remarks are retained; reactions are not used to infer public opinion, mobilization or quality.
deletionNotices: 王藤諺 is replying to a comment that has been deleted.
吳立志 is replying to a comment that has been deleted.
孫志貴 is replying to a comment that has been deleted.
孫志貴 is replying to a comment that has been deleted.
孫志貴 is replying to a comment that has been deleted.
郭超望 is replying to a comment that has been deleted.

items.author: Will 保哥的技術交流中心
items.replyLabel: Will 保哥的技術交流中心’s comment
items.title: The author links his separately published Traditional Chinese site
paragraphs: The author provides a link to his Traditional Chinese TOML website. It is a public entry point to his separately published translation, not evidence that upstream toml.io accepted or merged this PR.

evidenceLinks.label: The contributor’s Traditional Chinese site (not comprehensively assessed)

items.author: Yu-Fen Ceng
items.title: Distinguishing the tool debate from integrity
paragraphs: Yu-Fen Ceng says the reasons for requiring human translation could have been discussed directly in the PR. She instead criticizes asking AI to sound human and then taking the dispute to the page’s audience, characterizing these choices as deception and public shaming. She cites the maintainer’s conclusion that apparent tolerance of lying makes Traditional Chinese translations suspect, insists that tool use and integrity are separate issues, and states that some people do care about integrity.

The attachment is an English screenshot of the long reply in #99, highlighting accusations of dishonesty and suspicion toward future zh-TW translations. It verifies the wording she cites, but her criticism alone does not establish deliberate deception by the contributor.

items.author: 吳立志
items.title: Starting with maintenance costs and choosing to accommodate maintainers
paragraphs: 吳立志 argues that maintainers bear the actual costs and that a contributor cannot take responsibility for the wider problems caused by AI. He acknowledges a conflict but says he would choose to accommodate the maintainer’s position.

items.author: 觀月唯
items.title: Connecting the maintainer’s anger with the previous post’s tone
paragraphs: 觀月唯 says the wording of the author’s previous Facebook post explains why the maintainer would be upset. This assesses tone and reaction rather than independently establishing the maintainer’s actual state of mind.

items.author: Jack Aior
items.title: Participation means accepting a project’s tool restrictions
paragraphs: Jack Aior says some projects do not accept AI-generated results and that people wishing to participate must accept that requirement. This is a general contribution principle; he supplies no written policy source for this case.

items.author: 阮仕輔
items.title: Citing Forgejo’s position on AI submissions
paragraphs: 阮仕輔 cites Forgejo, saying its community opposes AI and that even AI-written issues violate its rules because of maintenance burdens. This is the commenter’s description of another project without a policy link. This chronicle has not used it to declare Forgejo’s current rules or TOML’s adopted policy.

items.author: Chun Yu Chen
items.title: Alleging broken support for existing locales
paragraphs: Chun Yu Chen alleges that the PR breaks existing language support in several places, says these should be fixed and uses that to explain rejection. The independently comparable technical finding here is Copilot’s English-fallback language-tag issue. No full regression test of every locale has been performed, so the wider allegation is not treated as wholly verified.

items.author: 張振豪
items.title: Responding to the author’s anger with emojis
paragraphs: 張振豪 says the author is angry, adding several laughing emojis, without new technical, review or policy evidence.

items.author: Shengan Lee
items.title: Finding human and AI writing harder to distinguish
paragraphs: Shengan Lee remarks that human writing is increasingly mistaken for AI while AI writing may be mistaken for human work. This general observation provides no verification of authorship or generation proportions in this case.

items.author: 陳冠霖
items.title: Explaining open-source caution through low-quality code
paragraphs: 陳冠霖 argues that many open-source projects have been traumatized by poor-quality code. He proposes a community background without examples establishing that it was the actual reason for this rejection.

items.author: 吳政達
items.title: A brush-writing analogy mocking tool restrictions
paragraphs: 吳政達 suggests asking the other party to start writing with a traditional brush before imposing tool requirements on others. This sarcastic analogy does not show that the author actually gave that response.

items.author: 朱家儀
items.title: Sharing a personal experience of rejected Chinese translation
paragraphs: 朱家儀 says she spent considerable time translating for a foreign open-source language project that welcomed contributions, only to be told Chinese was not mainstream or important and have her PR quickly closed. No project or PR link is given, so this is recorded as her experience rather than assumed to be the TOML incident.

items.author: Eric Theng
items.title: Predicting different futures for projects that support or oppose AI
paragraphs: Eric Theng predicts a divide between AI-supporting and AI-opposing camps. He expects supporters to iterate and improve rapidly and gain users, while opponents fix bugs slowly, lose users and eventually become dead projects. This prediction does not establish the quality, activity or future of this project.

items.author: 楊孟諺
items.title: A Taiwanese-language criticism of language barriers and broader changes
paragraphs: Writing in Taiwanese, 楊孟諺 says concern about unfamiliar-language content is natural and that this PR adds more than translation, making suspicion understandable. He also criticizes the author’s continued insistence on AI. The author later supplies a Mandarin rendering.

items.author: ChihKang Lin
items.title: Approving the term meat proxy
paragraphs: ChihKang Lin says he has learned the term meat proxy, interprets it as a carrier of AI output and praises its aptness. Approval of a label is not an independent investigation of the author’s workflow.

items.author: Wai Tang
items.title: Favoring doing it yourself and reporting confirmed bugs
paragraphs: Wai Tang supports doing the work oneself when dissatisfied and otherwise having little to say. Bugs should first be confirmed and then proactively reported. The original is brief; this chronicle does not extend it into approval of all behavior by either side.

items.author: Low Man Woei
items.title: A brief suggestion to ignore the other party
paragraphs: Low Man Woei briefly advises ignoring the other party, without reasons or new information about the incident.

items.author: Liu YuTang
items.title: Responding with a distinction between Taiwan and China
paragraphs: With a laughing tone, Liu YuTang says this is the time to emphasize that Taiwan is not China. The commenter’s political or regional distinction cannot establish the maintainer’s understanding of those places or motives for rejection.

items.author: 莊念迪
items.title: Reading the incident as an example of opposition to AI
paragraphs: 莊念迪 says he had only heard about anti-AI attitudes before but now has seen them firsthand. This is his characterization and reaction, without evidence beyond the underlying discussion.

items.author: Brune Kz
items.title: Suggesting several Taiwanese readers comment to attest to readability
paragraphs: Brune Kz suggests that more Taiwanese people comment to say that native speakers can understand the translation and get started easily. This verifiable invitation to comment belongs in the context of public amplification. It is this commenter’s suggestion, not proof that the author initiated or coordinated collective action or that anyone followed it.

items.author: 王哲驊
items.title: Questioning how the maintainer identified AI translation
paragraphs: 王哲驊 asks how the maintainer can distinguish AI translation. He suspects the PR may have been read but that judgment was made without reading the entire translation. This speculation cannot establish how much the maintainer inspected.

items.author: 周正泰
items.title: Speculating with political labels and possible regional misidentification
paragraphs: 周正泰 uses the disparaging political label “white left” and asks whether the maintainer mistook the author for someone from mainland China. These political and regional speculations lack direct evidence and are not verified motives.

items.author: 林昱廷
items.replyLabel: 林昱廷 replying to 周正泰’s comment
items.title: Replying with another political generalization
paragraphs: 林昱廷 replies to 周正泰 with a generalization that people labeled “white left” tend to like China. The political label is recorded without treating this generalization as fact or as evidence of the maintainer’s own position.

items.author: 黃光希
items.title: Generalizing about the number of anti-AI people
paragraphs: 黃光希 uses a derogatory term for people opposed to AI and says there are many of them now. This is an emotional group label, without new evidence relevant to the case.

items.author: 梁智峰
items.title: Describing personal complaints about rules and security
paragraphs: 梁智峰 describes being accused of rule violations, backing up documents, complaining to Google about security and seeking compensation. He says the incident harmed his wellbeing and development work. No supporting documents or concrete link to TOML are provided; the serious allegations remain his account.

items.author: Duke Hsu
items.title: Offering sympathy and good wishes
paragraphs: Duke Hsu recognizes the author’s effort and wishes him better luck, without a technical or policy argument.

items.author: 溫開水
items.title: Recommending the maintainer’s reply and other readers’ advice
paragraphs: 溫開水 recommends reading arp’s reply and other readers’ advice, linking 王韋傑’s comment on another post. The attachment shows the Facebook-linked confrontation in #99, closure and locking, and the long reply on human translation and zh-TW. It connects a public reminder with actual GitHub wording.

items.author: 朱立恆
items.replyLabel: 朱立恆 replying to 溫開水’s comment
items.title: Rendering the long reply from the locked issue in Chinese
paragraphs: Replying under 溫開水, 朱立恆 says the long text turns out to be the reply in #99, gives its permalink and renders the passages on mechanical translation, human review and suspicion of zh-TW into Traditional Chinese. The attachment is another Chinese presentation of the same reply.

He describes the lock as allowing no appeal. GitHub establishes that comments were restricted to collaborators at that time, not that every other channel for objection was unavailable. His translation is not a separate independent source of evidence.

items.author: Chun Yu Chen
items.title: Attachment 1: interface-label dictionaries and language-code mappings
paragraphs: Chun Yu Chen posts a code diff without additional written argument. It shows English and zh-TW interface labels, cn mapped to zh-CN and tw mapped to zh-TW. The presence of zh-CN alone does not mean Traditional Chinese is mislabeled, and the image cannot establish runtime behavior for every locale.

items.author: Baozi Xi
items.title: Sharing a social-media repost about Linus
paragraphs: Baozi Xi says Linus recently discussed a related issue and links an X post by Hesamation. This comment does not elaborate on the original content. The link is retained without independently checking the repost’s full original context or declaring Linus’s position on this TOML dispute.

evidenceLinks.label: The cited X repost (original context not verified)

items.author: 陳存善
items.title: Paraphrasing Linus on people who reject AI
paragraphs: 陳存善 says Linus stated that people who do not accept AI can fork or leave. No original source is provided. This is recorded as the commenter’s paraphrase, not a verified quotation or policy binding on TOML.

items.author: Chun Yu Chen
items.title: Attachment 2: language and label changes in navigation
paragraphs: Chun Yu Chen posts another navigation-template diff without further text. It shows a lang attribute added to the header and fixed labels such as Full spec and Language replaced with variables. This establishes changes to shared templates, not a complete functional test.

items.author: Chun Yu Chen
items.title: Attachment 3: specification container and menu-label changes
paragraphs: Chun Yu Chen posts a specification-template diff without written explanation. It shows lang added to the specification container and the fixed Menu label replaced by menuLabel, documenting shared-code changes beyond translated prose.

items.author: Chun Yu Chen
items.title: Asking for respect for the website maintainer
paragraphs: In a separate short comment, Chun Yu Chen emphasizes that it is the other party’s website and asks for respect. This is retained separately from his comments on code changes, rather than merged into one technical judgment.

items.author: Chun Yu Chen
items.title: Citing Copilot’s advice on English fallback labels
paragraphs: Chun Yu Chen says Copilot has already supplied a reason and attaches the review summary. The image concerns English fallback UI text inheriting a non-English lang attribute, potentially affecting screen-reader pronunciation. It matches the technical issue checked in this chronicle.

The review addresses interface language tags, not a finding that the entire Traditional Chinese translation is poor or confirmation of every reason for rejection. A separate fix commit exists, but #98 did not contain it at the captured cutoff.

items.author: Chun Yu Chen
items.title: Attachment 4: brlin-tw’s criticism and call to de-escalate
paragraphs: In a separate image-only comment, Chun Yu Chen reposts brlin-tw’s long response without adding text. The screenshot criticizes the submission method, lengthy PR description and move to Facebook, while also asking arp242 for actionable feedback, crediting the intention to contribute and urging de-escalation. It discloses LLM proofreading.
This repost is not counted as a new GitHub comment by brlin-tw. His full argument and the comparison with previous translation PRs are covered in the original record.

items.author: Pin-Han Huang
items.replyLabel: Pin-Han Huang replying to Yu-Fen Ceng’s comment
items.title: Criticizing an echo chamber and equating disagreement with anti-AI views
paragraphs: In Yu-Fen Ceng’s thread, Pin-Han Huang sees an echo chamber where lack of support is easily branded anti-AI, turning an engineering issue into something like political conflict. He argues that many open-source projects accept AI assistance and oppose work that increases costs. No statistics support that generalization about most projects.

items.author: Will 保哥的技術交流中心
items.replyLabel: Will 保哥的技術交流中心 replying to Yu-Fen Ceng’s comment
items.title: The author accepts criticism and acknowledges insufficient consideration
paragraphs: The author directly replies to Yu-Fen Ceng, accepts the criticism, acknowledges that he did not think things through, thanks her and says he will be more careful in his words and actions. This is a clear concession and conciliatory response. He does not itemize which accusations of deception, public shaming or mobilization he accepts, or say he will stop using AI.

items.author: Will 保哥的技術交流中心
items.replyLabel: Will 保哥的技術交流中心 replying to 吳立志’s comment
items.title: The author again asks for explicit contribution guidelines
paragraphs: In 吳立志’s thread, the author says his issue made clear that he would follow contribution guidelines if supplied. He believes the requirements were not written down, yet only human translation was later accepted. He notes that the second submission was an issue rather than a new PR and expresses puzzlement that it was still closed.

#99 is verifiably a new issue rather than a second PR. This reply cannot prove that no relevant rules existed anywhere. The checked README does not mention AI; that is different from saying no document or channel ever contained a rule.

items.author: 王藤諺
items.replyLabel: 王藤諺 replying to 吳立志’s comment
items.title: Connecting the GitHub profile with the Vibe Coder label
paragraphs: 王藤諺 alleges that the author’s entire GitHub profile is AI-generated and would therefore make arp242 see him as a Vibe Coder. This claim about the profile and another person’s perception supplies no complete generation-history evidence. It cannot establish that all previous work or this translation was generated by AI.
notes: A notice before this reply says the comment being replied to was deleted. Its top-level thread is known, but names, ordering and the notice do not establish the exact parent ID, deleted text, who removed it or why.

items.author: 吳立志
items.replyLabel: 吳立志 replying to 吳立志’s comment
items.title: Deriving decision rights from responsibility
paragraphs: In a reply mentioning 孫志貴, 吳立志 argues that responsibility gives the maintainer corresponding decision rights. Unless one can solve the maintainer’s problem, making a decision for him is intrusive. The platform also says the comment being replied to was deleted, preventing recovery of the full preceding exchange.
notes: A notice before this reply says the comment being replied to was deleted. Its top-level thread is known, but names, ordering and the notice do not establish the exact parent ID, deleted text, who removed it or why.

items.author: 孫志貴
items.replyLabel: 孫志貴 replying to 王藤諺’s comment
items.title: Asking whether a profile label justifies discriminatory treatment
paragraphs: 孫志貴 mentions 王藤諺 and asks whether that would justify such discriminatory treatment. He questions the move from an impression of a profile to how someone is treated. Calling the treatment discrimination remains his assessment.
notes: A notice before this reply says the comment being replied to was deleted. Its top-level thread is known, but names, ordering and the notice do not establish the exact parent ID, deleted text, who removed it or why.

items.author: 孫志貴
items.replyLabel: 孫志貴 replying to 郭超望’s comment
items.title: Acknowledging a misread username and a correction
paragraphs: Mentioning 郭超望, 孫志貴 admits misreading arp’s username and says he has corrected it. This correction of a name does not show withdrawal of all his views about policy and decision-making.
notes: A notice before this reply says the comment being replied to was deleted. Its top-level thread is known, but names, ordering and the notice do not establish the exact parent ID, deleted text, who removed it or why.

items.author: 孫志貴
items.replyLabel: 孫志貴 replying to 吳立志’s comment
items.title: Calling for an AI policy agreed by the maintenance team
paragraphs: 孫志貴 says the repository does not belong to arp242 alone and that he has tagged other maintainers to discuss it. He criticizes suspicion toward all future zh-Hant-TW localization PRs and asks for a collectively agreed AI policy rather than decisions by one member.
This statement cannot establish that a meeting actually occurred, that the team reached a decision or that policy changed. Repository permissions and formal governance are not fully presented here.
notes: A notice before this reply says the comment being replied to was deleted. Its top-level thread is known, but names, ordering and the notice do not establish the exact parent ID, deleted text, who removed it or why.

items.author: 郭超望
items.replyLabel: 郭超望 replying to 吳立志’s comment
items.title: Pointing out arp being written as alp
paragraphs: 郭超望 asks why someone keeps writing alp when the person’s username is arp. This is a correction of a name, not a new translation-quality judgment.
notes: A notice before this reply says the comment being replied to was deleted. Its top-level thread is known, but names, ordering and the notice do not establish the exact parent ID, deleted text, who removed it or why.

items.author: Will 保哥的技術交流中心
items.replyLabel: Will 保哥的技術交流中心 replying to Pin-Han Huang’s reply
items.title: The author continues to prioritize results over tools
paragraphs: Replying to Pin-Han Huang, the author says this is his first such experience and that most projects do not object to tools as long as results have quality. He focuses on what can be achieved rather than which tool is used. This view of tools and outcomes should be read separately from his later acceptance of Yu-Fen Ceng’s criticism of his handling.

items.author: Pin-Han Huang
items.replyLabel: Pin-Han Huang replying to Will 保哥的技術交流中心’s reply
items.title: Explaining rejection through low-quality output overwhelming review
paragraphs: Pin-Han Huang offers a possible bad-money-drives-out-good explanation: low-quality output can overwhelm review and lead to outright rejection. He compares academic journals and the difficulty of distinguishing AI-assisted work from pure Vibe output. These possibilities and analogies do not establish the maintainer’s complete actual motives.

items.author: Will 保哥的技術交流中心
items.replyLabel: Will 保哥的技術交流中心 replying to 陳冠霖’s comment
items.title: The author refers to unspecified well-known examples
paragraphs: Replying to 陳冠霖, the author briefly says it is really just those few well-known cases. He does not identify projects or people; this chronicle does not supply names on his behalf.

items.author: Will 保哥的技術交流中心
items.replyLabel: Will 保哥的技術交流中心 replying to 楊孟諺’s comment
items.title: The author renders the Taiwanese criticism into Mandarin
paragraphs: Replying to 楊孟諺, the author explicitly supplies a translation into Mandarin of the criticism about language barriers, changes beyond translation and insistence on AI. He adds no separate rebuttal in this comment. Posting a translation does not establish complete agreement with the criticism.

items.author: Qazplo Yao
items.replyLabel: Qazplo Yao replying to Brune Kz’s comment
items.title: Citing suspicion toward future zh-TW work and doubting contribution prospects
paragraphs: Replying to Brune Kz, Qazplo Yao quotes the maintainer’s English wording extending suspicion to future zh-TW translations and doubts that Traditional Chinese contributions remain possible. The passage actually comes from the long comment in #99, not a new PR ruling. Predicting that every future contribution is impossible goes beyond closure of this case.

items.author: 楊孟諺
items.replyLabel: 楊孟諺 replying to Chun Yu Chen’s comment
items.title: Emphasizing that the changes go beyond i18n
paragraphs: Under Chun Yu Chen’s template diff, 楊孟諺 says in Taiwanese that the issue indeed goes beyond i18n. This is a brief assessment of scope, without independent test results.
